sections.heading: The Bag That Becomes Walking Advertising
sections.text: Branded Retail Packaging The Bag That Becomes Walking Advertising A luxury paper gift bag is the most-seen piece of packaging you own — it leaves the store, walks the street, and re-enters homes. That is why boutiques, jewelers and fashion houses invest in a bag that feels as considered as the product inside. Our bags are built from heavyweight art paper or natural kraft (157–210gsm), reinforced at the base and top fold so handles never tear under weight. Choose cotton rope, satin ribbon, die-cut or twisted-paper handles, finished with matte soft-touch lamination, spot UV, deep emboss or gold foil for a tactile, premium pull. Produced in-house from printing to handle assembly, with tight colour control to keep your brand palette consistent across every reorder. Pair with our boxes and tissue for a complete, on-brand unboxing-to-carry experience.

sections.heading: Match the Handle to the Weight, Not to the Mood Board
sections.text: Load Engineering Match the Handle to the Weight, Not to the Mood Board Nearly every paper bag failure is the same failure: the handle was chosen for how it looked in the render, and the product turned out heavier than the render implied. Handle type is a load spec first and an aesthetic second. Handle Indicative load Where it belongs Die-cut (punched) Light only Cosmetics samples, cards, short carry from counter to car Twisted paper Roughly 5–8 kg (12–18 lb) depending on construction Apparel, everyday retail Cotton or nylon rope Roughly 15–25 kg Multi-item gifting, events, anything with glass or a boxed set inside Published ratings vary by supplier and construction — reported figures for twisted paper handles run from about 12 lb to 12 kg depending on cord diameter and how the handle is anchored, so treat any single number as a starting point and test at your real weight. The number that matters is not the handle's rating in isolation; it is the weakest link between handle, anchor patch and the paper it is glued to. Paper weight tracks the same ladder: roughly 70–90 gsm for light contents, 100–150 gsm for normal shopping loads, and 180–250 gsm with a reinforced bottom for heavy items . A rope handle on 90 gsm paper is a mismatch that fails at the anchor, not the rope — the cord stays intact and tears a neat hole through the wall on its way out. Worked example. A 16×8×24 cm boutique bag carrying a boxed candle set at about 1.2 kg is comfortably inside twisted-paper territory on paper. Put two of them in — 2.4 kg — and add a customer who swings the bag walking to the car, and the dynamic load at the anchor spikes well above the static weight. That is the case that comes back as a complaint. The fix is not a thicker bag: it is a rope handle with a reinforced top fold, which costs a little more per unit and removes the failure mode entirely.

sections.heading: The Three Reinforcements Nobody Specifies Until the Second Order
sections.text: Structural Detail The Three Reinforcements Nobody Specifies Until the Second Order Brands usually specify size, paper, print and handle, then discover the rest after the first shipment comes back with photographs attached. These are the three that account for most of it. Bottom board. A loose card insert sitting in the base, sized to the footprint. Without it the base bows into a curve under weight, the bag stops standing on a retail counter, and the load concentrates at the bottom seam instead of spreading across it. This is the cheapest upgrade on the list and the one with the most visible effect. Top fold reinforcement. The mouth of the bag is folded back on itself, giving the handle anchor two thicknesses of paper to grip instead of one. This is what stops the tear-through described above. Eyelets or knots at the anchor. For rope handles, how the cord terminates inside the bag decides the ceiling. A knot spreads load over a wider patch than a bare glued end; an eyelet spreads it further still and survives repeated reuse. One counterintuitive note on lamination: matte film looks and feels more premium than gloss on a luxury bag, but film of either kind adds negligible tensile strength. If you are laminating for durability rather than looks, you are paying for the wrong thing — put the money into the bottom board and the top fold instead.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Questions Frequently Asked Questions What paper weight do you use for luxury gift bags? We use heavyweight art paper or natural kraft from 157gsm to 210gsm, with a folded top hem and optional cardboard base insert so handles and base hold up to weight without tearing. What handle options are available? Cotton rope, satin or grosgrain ribbon, twisted paper, flat paper, and die-cut punch-out handles — all color-matched to your brand and reinforced at the attachment points. What is the minimum order quantity for custom paper bags? Standard MOQ is 300 pcs for a custom size with full printing. We can discuss smaller premium pilot runs on request. Can you make eco-friendly recyclable paper bags? Yes. We offer FSC-certified kraft and art paper, paper or cotton handles, water-based coatings and soy-based inks for fully recyclable, plastic-free bags. Can the bags match my boxes for a complete set? Yes — we produce coordinated box, bag, tissue and ribbon sets in one factory with consistent colour control, so your whole packaging suite stays on-brand. Do you supply luxury gift bags wholesale to trade buyers? Yes. Trade buyers order these as luxury gift bags wholesale, trade luxury paper bags or luxury branded paper bags — all describing the same branded retail carrier covered on this page. The wording changes by market; the quotation does not. What determines it is the paper weight, handle option and order quantity set out in the questions above, plus print coverage and finish. What are luxury paper bags called in German, French, Spanish, Italian and Polish? German buyers search Papiertragetaschen — Papiertragetaschen Hersteller for a manufacturer, Papiertragetaschen B2B or Großhandel for trade supply. French buyers use sac papier luxe, with fabricant sac papier luxe or sur mesure. Spanish buyers use bolsas de papel personalizadas, with fabricante, fábrica or al por mayor. Italian buyers use shopper carta personalizzate, with produttore or produzione. Polish buyers use torby papierowe z nadrukiem, with producent or hurt. French and Italian buyers also search specifically for short runs — sac papier luxe petite quantité and shopper carta personalizzate piccole quantità — which is the same question as the minimum order quantity answered above. This site and all quotations are in English. Are you a luxury paper bag manufacturer, and how is the wholesale price set? Yes. LuxoPack makes custom luxury paper bags and gift bags in its Shenzhen factory, so the quote comes from production, not a reseller. The price per bag is set by paper weight (157–210gsm), handle type, print coverage and finish, and quantity; a custom size with full printing starts at 300 pcs. Send the bag size, paper, handle and quantity for a quote. Do you make custom gift bags and custom shopping bags with a logo? Yes. The same construction is ordered as custom gift bags, custom shopping bags or custom paper bags with logo; what changes is the handle and finish. Rope or ribbon handles with foil or embossed logos suit gift and boutique use, while twisted or flat paper handles on kraft suit retail shopping bags. MOQ is 300 pcs per custom size with full printing.
